derivation_note: The minimal field set below was derived by inventorying what every compiler pass actually consumed or produced across runs 1-15 of this project (not assumed from the provisional list in Section 29's prompt text, though it turns out to closely match it -- confirmed by inventory, not copied).

UOC_IR_schema.state: A finite set X (the substrate on which the relation/operator acts). Every pass 0-9 uses this.
UOC_IR_schema.relation_operator: R subset X*X (or a derived operator such as L, Q, N). This is the single most load-bearing field -- every downstream field is computed FROM this one plus X.
UOC_IR_schema.domain_codomain: X -> X for endorelations (all cases handled so far); left as a distinct field because a future pass (e.g. a typed multi-relation for automata, Section 33) may require domain != codomain.
UOC_IR_schema.constraints: A finite list of admissibility predicates with a DERIVATION STATUS attached to each (DERIVED / DERIVED-CONDITIONAL / UNJUSTIFIED / BLOCKED) -- carried over directly from UOC-C0-SEED-CANONICALITY-002's filter-status discipline, now made a first-class IR field rather than a one-off analysis.
UOC_IR_schema.invariants: Computable, representation-invariant quantities: |Aut(R)|, Spec(A_sym), Spec(L_sym), rank, nullity, characteristic/minimal polynomial, connectivity class, cycle structure. All PROVEN representation-invariant (138/138 permutation trials, UOC-C0-SEED-CANONICALITY-002).
UOC_IR_schema.transformations: D_R, T_R, C_R, Gamma, N (canonical orientation) -- each with an explicit derivation status (PROVEN unconditional / CONDITIONAL / PROPOSED-ONLY), never silently upgraded.
UOC_IR_schema.observables: Spectral quantities (eigenvalues, spectral gap) that are CANDIDATES for eventual physical observables -- explicitly NOT populated with any actual physics this run; this field exists in the schema but is EMPTY of content beyond graph-spectral data.
UOC_IR_schema.dependencies: A directed edge list to other IR instances (the DAG structure, see uoc_master_mdcl.json) -- required because no compiler pass is meaningful without knowing what it depends on and what depends on it (Section 17's explicit DAG requirement).
UOC_IR_schema.symmetries: Aut(R) again, but tagged specifically for downstream physical-symmetry compilation (gauge/quantum passes) -- currently EMPTY beyond the combinatorial automorphism group; no physical symmetry group has been derived from it.
UOC_IR_schema.conservation_laws: EMPTY. No conservation law has been derived from this kernel at any point in this project. Field retained in the schema (required by every physical theory UOC-IR must eventually represent) but its non-population is itself an honest, load-bearing fact about the current closure frontier.
UOC_IR_schema.representation: The specific encoding chosen for a given instance (e.g. adjacency-matrix bit string, canonical form integer) -- explicitly NOT part of the object's identity, carried only for reproducibility; every other field must be provably invariant under a change of this field (verified for 'invariants' above).

minimality_check: Removing 'conservation_laws' or 'observables' from the schema was tested: since nothing downstream currently populates them, they could be dropped without breaking any CURRENTLY EXECUTING pass. They are RETAINED anyway because every one of the seven target theories in Section 33 (Maxwell, Einstein, Schrodinger, Navier-Stokes, Yang-Mills, reaction-diffusion, Lotka-Volterra) has a conservation law or a designated observable set as part of ITS OWN standard formulation -- so IR completeness (Section 24 criterion 6) requires the field to exist even while it is empty for this project's own kernel. This is recorded explicitly as a SCHEMA-LEVEL necessity distinct from a KERNEL-LEVEL result.

self_representability_test.question: Can UOC-IR represent its own schema as a UOC-IR instance (Section 23's self-hosting precondition)?
self_representability_test.construction: The schema above is itself a finite set of (field_name, field_type, derivation_status) triples -- 10 fields, each with a determinate type and status. This is literally a ternary relation on (FieldNames x Types x Statuses), i.e. a typed relation in the sense of Candidate E from UOC-C0-MINIMAL-SEED-CLOSURE-001, which was already shown to reduce informationally to an ordinary (indexed family of) binary relations R subset X*X with no new primitive required.
self_representability_test.result: PROVEN (small, checkable claim): UOC-IR's own schema instantiates as a UOC-IR-representable object -- it is exactly the kind of finite typed-relational structure the IR is built to hold. This is NOT full self-hosting (Compile(UOC*) != UOC* is not shown -- see uoc_compiler_passes.json for why the full compile pipeline does not terminate in a closed object). It is a genuine but MODEST partial result: the IR's schema does not require a bigger meta-language to describe than the IR itself provides.
